At last night's Emmy Awards ceremony, Apple TV+ beat out competitors including HBO to become the platform with the most wins. Below is HBO's Casey Bloys' response to Apple TV+'s victory.

The HBO CEO highly praised Apple TV+'s outstanding performance, but also acknowledged that competing with a trillion-dollar company is "quite challenging."

Apple TV+ has long been compared to HBO, with both prioritising quality over quantity. Apple has even sometimes been called "the new HBO."

Last night's Emmy Awards further cemented that notion, with Apple TV+ surpassing HBO, Netflix and other platforms to become the platform with the most wins that evening.

Apple TV+ won a total of 29 awards, becoming the "most awarded network of the year," with shows like Widow's Bay performing particularly well. HBO came in second with 21 awards.

After the Emmy Awards ceremony, HBO executive Casey Bloys was interviewed by Deadline and asked for his thoughts on Apple TV+'s performance. Here's his response:

DEADLINE: What do you think of Apple TV+'s performance this time? They've become the most awarded platform at the Emmys for the first time — what are your thoughts? BLOYS: I'm actually quite happy, because I think they're a very strong competitor, Zack and Jamie. We've always had strong competitors — Showtime, FX, AMC, Netflix, Amazon — so having Apple there keeps everyone on their toes, and that's actually when I perform at my best. They're a trillion-dollar company, and that is indeed quite challenging, but we'll keep doing what we've always done, which is making the best shows.

Bloys joined HBO in 2004 and has served as head of programming since 2016. His track record speaks for itself, and his response to Apple TV+'s win was largely gracious, offering sincere congratulations.

However, the most interesting part of his response was this line: "They're a trillion-dollar company, and that is indeed quite challenging."

We don't know exactly what Apple TV+'s internal budget is, but there's no question that Apple's overall financial resources far exceed those of most competitors, including HBO.

Coincidentally, Paramount is currently actively seeking to acquire HBO (along with other Warner Bros. Discovery assets), hoping to compete more effectively with tech giants like Apple and Amazon.

Does being big naturally bring advantages? Perhaps. But many TV networks have proven that when it comes to making content audiences love, money is only a small part of the equation.

Apple TV+ costs $14.99 per month, and is also available through the Apple One bundle subscription service.
